subsystems.name: Driver (transducer)
subsystems.role: converts the electrical audio signal into sound; almost all headsets use a moving-coil dynamic driver, with balanced-armature or planar-magnetic types in premium models.
parts: neodymium magnet and steel pole pieces

subsystems.name: Earcup and acoustic enclosure
subsystems.role: the sealed or vented cavity behind and in front of the driver shapes bass response and blocks outside noise.

subsystems.name: Microphone
subsystems.role: captures the voice; a boom-mounted capsule on gaming headsets, or an array of tiny MEMS mics built into the cups for calls and noise cancellation.

subsystems.name: Electronics and signal chain
subsystems.role: amplifies, converts and, for wireless models, encodes and decodes the audio.
parts: Bluetooth radio and codec chip (or USB controller)

subsystems.name: Active noise cancellation (optional)
subsystems.role: samples outside and inside noise with microphones and plays an inverted copy to cancel it.

subsystems.name: Headband and mechanical structure
subsystems.role: holds the cups at a consistent seal against the ears, which the acoustics depend on.

buildSteps.title: Design the acoustics
buildSteps.detail: Engineers model the driver, cup volume and vents together, then set a target frequency-response curve for the intended use.

buildSteps.title: Build the drivers
buildSteps.detail: A voice coil of fine enamelled copper wire is wound and bonded to the diaphragm; the magnet assembly, pole pieces and surround are assembled, and the coil is centred in the magnetic gap.

buildSteps.title: Mould the shell and headband
buildSteps.detail: Cup shells and headband parts are injection moulded in ABS or polycarbonate; the headband spring is formed from steel or composite and cushioned.

buildSteps.title: Assemble the pads
buildSteps.detail: Foam is cut or moulded, wrapped in protein leather, velour or fabric, and sewn or heat-sealed to a mounting ring.

buildSteps.title: Build the microphone
buildSteps.detail: A MEMS die is soldered to a circuit board with its preamp, or an electret capsule is wired into the boom; the boom is assembled with its gooseneck and windscreen.

buildSteps.title: Populate the circuit boards
buildSteps.detail: The DAC, amplifier, ADC, radio module and power circuitry are surface-mounted, and firmware is flashed.

buildSteps.title: Assemble and seal the headset
buildSteps.detail: The driver is glued or clipped into the cup with its damping material, wires are routed, the mic is connected, and the cup is closed so the seal behaves as designed.

buildSteps.title: Test and tune
buildSteps.detail: Each unit is measured on a head-and-torso simulator and in an anechoic chamber to check frequency response, left-right matching and mic sensitivity; noise-cancellation filters are tuned per model.

prerequisites.why: the basic transducer physics and manufacturing have been mature for about a century.
small, light, strong magnets are what make headphone-sized drivers loud and efficient.
wafer-scale silicon mics are cheap, tiny and consistent enough for mic arrays.
wireless headsets need a codec and radio that can run for many hours on a small battery.

prerequisites.tech: Real-time digital signal processing for ANC
prerequisites.why: cancellation needs a filter that reacts to noise within microseconds on a low-power chip.

pathway.milestone: wired and Bluetooth headsets with active noise cancellation and multi-mic voice pickup
pathway.unlocks: clear calls and immersive gaming in noisy rooms.

pathway.milestone: LE Audio with the LC3 codec and Auracast broadcast, plus lower-latency game modes
pathway.unlocks: better quality at lower bitrate and one transmitter feeding many headsets.

pathway.milestone: head-tracked spatial audio with personalised hearing profiles
pathway.unlocks: sound that stays fixed in space as the head turns, and tuning to the listener's own ears.

pathway.milestone: on-device AI speech enhancement and biometric sensing built into the headset
pathway.unlocks: voice isolation in very loud environments and continuous health signals from the ear.
